Title_1: Chili-Lime Edamame and Sweet Corn Salad
Introduction_1: Forget waiting for a pot to boil; combining two colorful freezer staples with a bright citrus dressing creates a satisfying, high-fiber side without the stove.
Ingredient_2_1: 1/2 cup (82 g) Frozen sweet corn kernels
Ingredient_3_1: 1/4 cup (40 g) Red onion, finely chopped
Instruction_1_1: Place the edamame and sweet corn in a microwave-safe bowl.
Instruction_2_1: Microwave on high for 2 to 3 minutes, checking halfway, until both vegetables are completely thawed and just warmed through.
Instruction_3_1: Drain any excess water from the bowl to prevent a soggy salad.
Instruction_4_1: Add the red onion, olive oil, lime juice, and chili powder to the warmed vegetables.
Instruction_5_1: Toss everything well to coat the edamame and corn evenly in the dressing.
Instruction_6_1: Stir in the chopped cilantro just before serving or storing.
Variation_1: Swap the chili powder for ground cumin and smoked paprika.
Storage_1: Keeps 2 to 3 days refrigerated in an airtight container.
Title_2: Citrus and Pistachio Shaved Brussels Sprouts Slaw
Introduction_2: This simple no-cook slaw requires minimal prep and uses convenient ingredients. Pre-shaved Brussels sprouts tenderize perfectly when tossed with fresh orange segments and a tangy vinaigrette.
Ingredient_7_2: 7 oz (200 g) Bagged shaved Brussels sprouts
Ingredient_8_2: 1 oz (30 g) Shelled pistachios, roughly chopped
Instruction_1_2: Whisk the extra-virgin olive oil, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and black pepper in a large mixing bowl until smooth.
Instruction_2_2: Cut the peeled orange into bite-sized segments and discard any seeds.
Instruction_3_2: Add the shaved Brussels sprouts and orange segments to the bowl with the dressing.
Instruction_4_2: Toss the salad thoroughly and massage the Brussels sprouts to help them absorb the liquid and soften.
Instruction_6_2: Sprinkle the chopped pistachios over the slaw before serving.
Variation_2: Swap the orange segments for diced crisp green apple.
Storage_2: Keeps 2-3 days refrigerated; add pistachios just before serving.

Title_1: Garlicky Spinach and Brown Rice Pilaf
Introduction_1: Providing steady complex carbohydrates and fiber, this quick side dish helps keep energy levels stable between meals. It transforms simple brown rice with fresh spinach, bright lemon, and crunchy walnuts into an effortless, vegetable-heavy plate.
Ingredient_3_1: 6 oz (170 g) Fresh baby spinach, roughly chopped
Ingredient_4_1: 1 cup (150 g) Ready-to-eat cooked brown rice pouch
Instruction_1_1: Heat the extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering.
Instruction_2_1: Add the garlic and sauté for 30 to 60 seconds until fragrant but not browned. Check at 30 seconds.
Instruction_3_1: Add the baby spinach in handfuls, tossing constantly for 1 to 2 minutes until fully wilted. Check at 1 minute.
Instruction_4_1: Stir in the cooked brown rice, breaking up any clumps. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until heated through. Check at 2 minutes.
Instruction_5_1: Remove the skillet from the heat.
Instruction_6_1: Stir in the lemon zest, lemon juice, chopped walnuts, and black pepper.
Instruction_7_1: Divide the pilaf between plates and serve warm.
Variation_1: Swap the chopped walnuts for toasted pine nuts or almonds.
Storage_1: Keeps 2 to 3 days refrigerated; reheat in the microwave.
Title_2: Hummus, Crispbread, and Vegetable Snack Plates
Introduction_2: A balance of plant protein, healthy fats, and complex carbohydrates provides steady afternoon energy without a blood sugar spike. Plenty of fresh vegetables and whole grains deliver lasting fullness.
Ingredient_6_2: 1/2 tsp (1 g) Za'atar seasoning or dried oregano
Instruction_1_2: Divide the hummus evenly between two snack plates or airtight meal-prep containers.
Instruction_2_2: Arrange one crispbread slice, the prepared cucumber, cherry tomatoes, and almonds around the hummus on each plate.
Instruction_3_2: Sprinkle the za'atar or oregano evenly over the hummus and the fresh vegetables.
Instruction_4_2: Drizzle the lemon juice lightly over the vegetables just before serving.
Variation_2: Swap the almonds for raw unsalted walnuts or pumpkin seeds.
Storage_2: Keeps 2 days refrigerated in an airtight container.

Introduction_1: Provides a satisfying hit of lean protein to keep energy steady and easily bridge the gap between meals. Thawing ready-to-eat shrimp under cold water creates an instant, refreshing plate with plenty of crisp crunch.
Ingredient_1_1: 4 oz (115 g) Frozen cooked shrimp (untreated, peeled, tail-off)
Ingredient_2_1: 5 oz (150 g) English cucumber, sliced into thick rounds
Ingredient_3_1: 1.3 oz (38 g) Low-sodium whole-wheat woven crackers
Ingredient_6_1: 1 tbsp (3 g) Fresh dill, finely chopped
Instruction_1_1: Place the frozen shrimp in a colander and run under cold water for 5 to 7 minutes until completely thawed.
Instruction_2_1: Transfer the thawed shrimp to paper towels and pat them thoroughly dry.
Instruction_3_1: Chop the shrimp roughly into small, bite-sized pieces so they will easily balance on the crackers.
Instruction_4_1: Transfer the chopped shrimp to a small bowl and toss with the lemon juice, olive oil, fresh dill, and black pepper.
Instruction_5_1: Arrange the crackers on a serving plate.
Instruction_6_1: Top each cracker with a cucumber round and a spoonful of the herbed shrimp mixture.
Variation_1: Swap the dill for chopped fresh cilantro and a lime squeeze.
Storage_1: Best enjoyed right away to keep the crackers completely crisp.
Title_2: Lemony Black-Eyed Pea and Tomato Salad
Introduction_2: When you need a fast afternoon snack or a vegetable side for a weeknight dinner, this crisp marinated bean salad works perfectly. The lemon and oregano dressing pairs easily with grilled or roasted mains.
Ingredient_1_2: 1 cup (160 g) Canned no-salt-added black-eyed peas, rinsed and drained
Ingredient_4_2: 1/4 cup (30 g) Red onion, finely chopped
Instruction_1_2: Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, oregano, salt, and black pepper together in a medium bowl.
Instruction_2_2: Add the black-eyed peas, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and parsley to the bowl.
Instruction_3_2: Toss the salad until all ingredients are coated in the dressing.
Variation_2: Swap the fresh parsley for chopped fresh dill or mint.
Storage_2: Keeps 2 to 3 days refrigerated in an airtight container.

Title_1: Mediterranean Lentil Salad Stuffed Mini Peppers
Introduction_1: Using sweet pepper halves as edible scoops turns a hearty, fiber-rich lentil salad into a satisfying finger food.
Ingredient_2_1: 8.5 oz (240 g) No-salt-added canned brown lentils, rinsed and drained
Ingredient_3_1: 2.8 oz (80 g) Fresh cucumber, finely diced
Ingredient_4_1: 0.7 oz (20 g) Kalamata olives, finely chopped
Instruction_1_1: Halve the mini sweet peppers lengthwise and scoop out the seeds and membranes to create hollow boats.
Instruction_2_1: Whisk the olive oil, red wine vinegar, dried oregano, and black pepper in a medium mixing bowl.
Instruction_3_1: Fold the lentils, cucumber, and olives into the dressing and toss to coat the ingredients evenly.
Instruction_4_1: Spoon the lentil mixture into the hollowed sweet pepper halves and serve.
Variation_1: Swap the dried oregano for freshly chopped mint or dill.
Storage_1: Keeps 2 days refrigerated; store the peppers and filling separately.
Title_2: Parmesan and Pistachio Olive Oil Popcorn
Introduction_2: Bringing Mediterranean ingredients to a movie-night classic turns a simple whole grain into a savory, fiber-rich snack. Popping the corn in olive oil and tossing it with crushed pistachios delivers a satisfying crunch that supports steady blood sugar.
Ingredient_1_2: 1/4 cup (30 g) Shelled pistachios, roughly chopped
Instruction_1_2: Heat the extra-virgin olive oil in a large pot with a tight-fitting lid over medium-high heat. Drop in the test popcorn kernels.
Instruction_2_2: Add the remaining popcorn kernels when the test kernels pop. Cover the pot and remove from the heat for 30 seconds to equalize the temperature.
Instruction_3_2: Return the pot to medium heat.
Instruction_4_2: Shake the pot continuously as the corn pops for 2 to 4 minutes. Check the progress at 2 minutes, and stop shaking when the popping slows to one pop every 2 to 3 seconds.
Instruction_5_2: Remove the pot from the heat immediately. Add the chopped pistachios, grated parmesan cheese, garlic powder, dried thyme, and black pepper directly into the hot pot.
Instruction_6_2: Toss the mixture well so the residual heat warms the nuts and helps the cheese stick.
Instruction_7_2: Transfer the popcorn to a large bowl and serve warm.
Variation_2: Trade the dried thyme for a pinch of smoked paprika.
Storage_2: Best enjoyed right away; does not keep.

Title_1: Roasted Red Pepper and Walnut Dip
Introduction_1: An ideal mid-afternoon snack to bridge the gap until dinner, this Mediterranean spread recreates the rich flavors of muhammara without the wait. Walnuts lend a creamy body to the dip while providing supportive omega-3 fatty acids.
Ingredient_1_1: 3/4 cup (120 g) Jarred roasted red peppers, no-salt-added, rinsed and drained well
Ingredient_9_1: 1 small pita (50 g) Whole-wheat pita bread, cut into wedges
Ingredient_10_1: 1 medium (200 g) Cucumber, sliced into thick rounds
Instruction_1_1: Place the drained roasted red peppers, walnuts, garlic, lemon juice, extra-virgin olive oil, cumin, red pepper flakes, and salt into a small food processor or blender.
Instruction_2_1: Blend on high speed until smooth, scraping down the sides of the bowl with a spatula as needed.
Instruction_3_1: Transfer the dip to a small serving bowl.
Instruction_4_1: Arrange the cucumber rounds and whole-wheat pita wedges on a plate alongside the dip.
Instruction_5_1: Serve immediately using the cucumber and pita to scoop up the dip.
Variation_1: Swap the cucumber slices for crisp celery or carrot sticks.
Storage_1: Keeps 3-4 days refrigerated in an airtight container.
Title_2: Rosemary Almond and Pepita Mix with Pear
Introduction_2: This fast and simple snack requires just a single skillet. Raw almonds and pumpkin seeds are toasted with savory herbs and served alongside fresh pear for an enjoyable crunch.
Ingredient_4_2: 1 tsp (2 g) Fresh rosemary, finely chopped
Ingredient_7_2: 1 medium (180 g) Fresh pear, cored and sliced
Instruction_1_2: Combine the almonds, pumpkin seeds, olive oil, rosemary, garlic powder, and salt in a small bowl and stir until evenly coated.
Instruction_2_2: Heat a medium dry skillet over medium heat.
Instruction_3_2: Add the nut mixture to the skillet and toast for 4 to 6 minutes. Stir frequently, checking at 4 minutes, until the seeds begin to pop and smell fragrant.
Instruction_4_2: Remove the skillet from the heat and immediately transfer the hot nut mixture to a plate to prevent burning.
Instruction_5_2: Divide the sliced pear between two plates and serve alongside the warm toasted nuts.
Variation_2: Swap the sliced pear for a crisp Granny Smith apple.
Storage_2: Store leftover cooled nuts up to 3 days at room temperature.

Title_1: Smoky Butter Bean Dip with Sweet Peppers
Introduction_1: Silky and boldly spiced, this creamy dip uses tender butter beans to create a satisfying, high-fiber snack.
Ingredient_1_1: 5 oz (150 g) Canned no-salt-added butter beans, rinsed and drained
Ingredient_5_1: 1 tbsp (10 g) Unsalted roasted pumpkin seeds (pepitas)
Ingredient_6_1: 1 clove (3 g) Garlic, peeled and smashed
Ingredient_9_1: 3 oz (80 g) Red bell pepper, sliced into strips
Ingredient_10_1: 2 oz (60 g) Carrots, cut into sticks
Instruction_1_1: Place the butter beans, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, smoked paprika, and salt in a food processor or blender.
Instruction_2_1: Blend on high speed until completely smooth and creamy, pulsing in the water if the mixture is too thick.
Instruction_3_1: Transfer the dip to a serving bowl.
Instruction_4_1: Garnish the surface with the roasted pumpkin seeds.
Instruction_5_1: Serve immediately alongside the red bell pepper and carrots for dipping.
Variation_1: Trade the smoked paprika for ground cumin and fresh cilantro.
Storage_1: Keeps up to 3 days refrigerated in an airtight container.
Title_2: Warm Cinnamon-Berry Greek Yogurt Bowls with Toasted Oats
Introduction_2: This simple six-ingredient snack is completely ready in under ten minutes. A warm compote of frozen mixed berries and cinnamon perfectly complements chilled nonfat Greek yogurt and freshly toasted oats.
Ingredient_1_2: 1 1/2 cups (340 g) Nonfat plain Greek yogurt
Instruction_1_2: Place a small, dry skillet over medium heat. Add the oats and sliced almonds.
Instruction_2_2: Toast the mixture, stirring frequently, for 3 to 5 minutes until golden and fragrant. Check at 3 minutes to prevent burning, then transfer to a small dish to cool.
Instruction_3_2: Place the frozen berries in a microwave-safe bowl. Microwave on high for 1 to 2 minutes until hot and juicy, checking at 1 minute.
Instruction_4_2: Mash the warm berries slightly with a fork to release their natural syrup. Stir in the cinnamon and vanilla extract.
Instruction_5_2: Divide the yogurt between two serving bowls.
Instruction_6_2: Spoon the warm berry compote over the yogurt and top with the toasted oat and almond crunch.
Variation_2: Swap the mixed berries for frozen dark sweet cherries.
Storage_2: Best enjoyed right away; does not keep.
